title: Rigidified Picard representability for proper geometrically integral algebraic-space families
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and $f:X\to S$ a proper flat finitely presented algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] with geometrically integral fibres and a section $e:S\to X$. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. A line module is an $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$-module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every $S$-scheme $T$ the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism. The functor assigning to $T$ the isomorphism classes of pairs $(M,r)$ with $M$ a line module on $X_T$ and $r:e_T^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_T$ is represented by a separated commutative group algebraic space $P\to S$ locally of finite presentation, with group law tensor product. Any automorphism of $(M,r)$ is the identity. The same classification and uniqueness apply to algebraic-space parameters $T$. There is a universal rigidified line module on $X\times_SP$, also when the parameter $P$ is an algebraic space. The zero section represents the trivial rigidified module. This representation and the universal module commute with arbitrary scheme base change. The geometric fibre $P_{\bar s}$ represents the ordinary rigidified Picard functor of $X_{\bar s}$.

Universal family over an algebraic-space parameter is etale descent of rigidified line modules.

proof.text: A nonempty integral geometric fibre is reduced and irreducible, hence connected. Apply [lem-sfb-space-geometric-h0] to $f$. It gives the canonical structure-sheaf isomorphism for every scheme parameter and, in fact, every algebraic-space parameter. Apply [lem-sfb-space-picard-sheaf-representability] to obtain a quasi-separated locally finitely presented commutative group algebraic space $P$ representing the fppf sheafification of $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$. This application uses properness, flatness, finite presentation and precisely the universal structure-sheaf isomorphism just proved; it does not require $X$ to be a scheme.

For any parameter $T$, a module endomorphism of a line module is locally multiplication by a function in a frame. Changing a frame conjugates by a unit, so leaves this function unchanged. These functions therefore glue to a global function; automorphisms correspond exactly to global units. By Step 1 every such unit on $X_T$ is the pullback of a unique unit on $T$, and pulling back along $e_T$ recovers that unit. Thus an automorphism preserving a rigidification is multiplication by $1$. Two rigidification-preserving isomorphisms, if they exist, are equal. For any line module $M$ define $N(M)=M\otimes f_T^*(e_T^*M)^{-1}$ with its evaluation rigidification at $e_T$. This kills every base pullback: $N(M\otimes f_T^*B)\simeq N(M)$ canonically, and if $(M,r)$ was rigidified then evaluation using $r$ gives $N(M)\simeq M$ preserving rigidifications. These formulas commute with pullback because they are formulas for tensor product, duals and evaluation.

source.place: Tags 0D28 and 0D2B, explicit scalar correction and automorphism calculation

proof.text: For a scheme $T$ let $R(T)$ be the rigidified isomorphism classes. A matching family for an fppf cover has unique rigidified overlap isomorphisms by Step 2, so these satisfy the cocycle. The pulled-back cover of $X_T$ is fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Each line module is quasi-coherent: on a local frame it has the presentation $0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\sim}M\to0$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] to descend to a quasi-coherent module; [lem-sfb-space-fppf-invertible-locality] makes it a line module. Full faithfulness on $T$ descends the compatible section trivializations and their inverses. Thus $R$ is an fppf sheaf. Normalization gives a map from the Picard presheaf to $R$ and hence from its sheafification. Forgetting rigidification gives the reverse map. The first composite differs from a Picard presheaf class by $f_T^*e_T^*M$, which is locally trivial and hence zero in the sheafification; the other composite is identity by the rigidified isomorphism $N(M)\simeq M$. Thus $P(T)\simeq R(T)$ naturally. Tensor product gives the group law; zero is the trivial module with identity rigidification.

source.place: Tag 0D28, normalization and effective descent; Tag 0D2B; spaces-descent.tex Tags 04W8 and 060X

proof.text: To prove separatedness let $R$ be any valuation ring with fraction field $K$, and let two $R$-points of $P$ agree over $K$. By Step 3 choose their rigidified representatives $(M,r)$ and $(M_2,r_2)$. Their tensor difference $L=M\otimes(M_2)^{-1}$ is trivial on $X_K$. The generic-triviality theorem [lem-sfb-space-valuation-line-triviality] applies to the base-changed family, which is proper flat and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]: its geometric fibres are the geometric fibres in the original hypothesis. It gives an unrigidified trivialization $L\simeq\mathcal O_{X_R}$. Its pullback to the section differs from the specified rigidification of $L$ by a unit of $R$; multiplying by the inverse of this unit corrects it. Thus the two rigidified classes agree over $R$. Since Step 1 gives a quasi-compact diagonal, [lem-sfb-space-valuative-separatedness] now proves that $P\to S$ is separated. This argument uses all valuation rings, with no discrete or Noetherian restriction.

Let $T$ be an algebraic-space parameter. Fibre products and base-changed etale covers exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to T$; its overlaps are schemes by the representable diagonal [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A map $T\to P$ gives scheme-parameter rigidified modules on $X_U$ with matching overlap classes by Step 3. Their unique rigidified isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle by Step 2. The cover $X_U\to X_T$ is fppf by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. The line modules are quasi-coherent by their local rank-one presentations [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], so [lem-sfb-space-fppf-qcoh-descent] descends them to a quasi-coherent module. It is a line module by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-invertible-locality]. Full faithfulness on $U\to T$ descends the section trivialization and its inverse. Conversely a rigidified module on $X_T$ gives an atlas map $U\to P$ agreeing on overlaps; these maps descend uniquely since $P$ is an etale sheaf. These constructions are inverse and independent of atlas refinement by unique descent; uniqueness of rigidified isomorphisms is checked on $U$. At $T=P$, the identity map therefore gives a universal rigidified module on $X\times_SP$ whose pullbacks are the classified modules.

source.place: Tags 04W8 and 060X, descent of the universal rigidified module; spaces.tex Tag 025Y

proof.text: For any scheme base change $S_1\to S$, a scheme over $S_1$ has the same fibre product family, section, line modules and rigidifications whether evaluated relative to $S$ or $S_1$. The classification just proved therefore identifies $P\times_SS_1$ with the representing space for that family, naturally on all scheme tests. The pulled-back universal module classifies the identity under this identification, so it is isomorphic to the universal module there by Step 5, uniquely as a rigidified module by Step 2. Identity and iterated base-change comparisons consequently agree. This proves arbitrary scheme base-change compatibility even when $S_1$ is not locally Noetherian. Taking $S_1=\bar s$ yields the ordinary rigidified Picard functor of the geometric fibre, with its universal module.
